ai.title: Reorganize docs, promote Troubleshooting to Advanced section
ai.summary: Troubleshooting guide moves from `help` to `advanced` section with `order: 1`, becoming the first advanced doc. `what-models.mdx` and `large-projects.mdx` shift to orders 3 and 4 respectively. FAQ and getting-started pages now link to `/docs/advanced/troubleshooting`. Model list in `what-models.mdx` adds Gemini 2.5 Pro for deep thinking, removes previous Claude Sonnet-only coding description.

eli5.text: The troubleshooting guide that used to live at the bottom of the help section has been moved to the front of the advanced guides, so anyone browsing for solutions to install or running problems will now see it as the first item under advanced docs. The two companion articles about which models are used and how to work on large projects shifted down by one spot, and both the FAQ and the getting-started page now point readers directly to the relocated troubleshooting article. You might also notice the troubleshooting section's opening checklist has been rewritten from a plain bullet list into grouped steps with bold headings for checking the Node version, fixing permission errors, and next steps if problems persist. Live today: the guide is already moved, but it only affects people who click

ai.title: Silence npm-app build output in start script
ai.summary: The npm-app start script pipes nx build output to /dev/null. This reduces local dev verbosity. Affects npm-app/package.json scripts only.

eli5.text: When you start your local assistant using the normal start command, a lot of technical build messages no longer print to your screen while it compiles. Instead, those messages are sent to an internal black hole that discards them, so your terminal stays quiet until the actual assistant launches. This makes the startup experience cleaner and less noisy for anyone running the assistant locally. The change only affects how the start command is run, nothing about what the assistant does afterward.

ai.title: Fix SWE-Bench evals and analytics init
ai.summary: Refactored `passesSweBenchTests` to use `spawn` for streaming output and resolving async results instead of `execSync` with grep. Moved analytics client initialization check to occur after non-production logging to prevent unnecessary throws. Added `setProjectRoot` and `setWorkingDirectory` to `setupTestEnvironment` in `test-setup.ts`. Scope covers `common/src/analytics.ts`, `evals/swe-bench-eval.ts`, and `evals/test-setup.ts`.

eli5.text: When running automated tests that check whether the assistant's code fixes actually work, the test runner now watches the testing process live and waits for the final result instead of blindly grepping output after it finished, so failures and hangs are caught more reliably. The analytics system also stops logging dummy events during local development before it complains about a missing analytics connection, so developers won't see confusing errors while testing. These changes only affect the project's internal testing and analytics setup, so regular users won't notice anything different today.

ai.title: SWE-bench eval patch rundocker.py git safe.directory
ai.summary: Added patchRunDockerScript in evals/test-setup.ts to inject git config --global --add safe.directory '*' into run_docker.py docker_command. Fixes SWE-bench eval failures from git ownership checks in Docker. Scope: Evals, swe-bench-eval.ts, test-setup.ts.

eli5.text: When the system runs automated tests inside isolated containers, those containers start up as a different computer user, which trips a built-in Git safety check that blocks file access and makes the tests fail. The fix tells Git to ignore that ownership rule for the repository folder so the tests can run normally. If you looked, you would see the test setup step now silently configures Git before launching the containers. It is live now for anyone running these automated evaluation tests.

ai.title: CI setup refactored to use composite action
ai.summary: GitHub Actions setup moved to composite action .github/actions/setup-job/action.yml. Removed inline checkout, Bun setup, and caching steps from ci.yml build job. Environment variable CODEBUFF_GITHUB_ACTIONS now set globally in workflow env instead of appending to .env.local during setup.

eli5.text: The build system used by the project's automated checks was reorganized so the setup steps live in one reusable place instead of being copied into every check. If you watched the checks run, you'd see them start faster and behave more consistently, because they now pull from a single shared setup instead of each defining its own checkout, dependency installation, and caching. The special flag that tells the software it's running inside the automated system is now set at the top level for all checks, rather than being written into a settings file during setup. This is internal plumbing; nothing about the product you use changes as a result.

ai.title: Add explicit checkout to CI jobs
ai.summary: Added `actions/checkout@v3` to build, npm-app tests, backend tests, and common tests jobs in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`. Ensures repository is available before local action `./.github/actions/setup-job` runs. Aligns CI setup with local execution requirements.

eli5.text: If you trigger the project's automated checks (the ones that run when someone sends in new code), those checks will now reliably find the project's own setup scripts before doing anything else. You wouldn't see a difference as a user; this just keeps the behind-the-scenes testing steps from failing silently when they couldn't locate shared helper scripts.

ai.title: setup-job action writes .env.local
ai.summary: The `setup-job` GitHub Action now writes `.env.local` with `ENV_LOCAL` and `CODEBUFF_GITHUB_ACTIONS=true`. This ensures credentials and flags are available for CI tests. Scope: `.github/actions/setup-job/action.yml`. Detail: Appends flag to file after writing env vars.

eli5.text: The automated testing setup now quietly creates a small configuration file that holds secret login-like values and a special flag so the tests can run properly. If you peek at the testing process, you'd see this file being written out with those values before the real tests begin. This affects anyone watching or debugging the project's automated checks, which are now passing again after a brief hiccup.

ai.title: CI workflow injects ENVLOCAL and CODEBUFF flag
ai.summary: The `ci.yml` workflow now creates a `.env.local` file before installing dependencies. It writes the `ENV_LOCAL` secret and appends `CODEBUFF_GITHUB_ACTIONS=true`. This ensures the test environment has the required credentials and flag during CI runs.

eli5.text: When the project runs its automated checks, it now quietly creates a small setup file that holds a secret credential and a flag telling the system it's running in an automated environment. This only matters during that automated testing process, which engineers use to make sure new code doesn't break things; regular users won't see anything change. The credential and flag are only present during these checks and aren't used by the main application.

ai.title: Fix CI credential retrieval and deduplicate setup
ai.summary: Updated .github/actions/setup-job/action.yml to read credentials from secrets.ENV_LOCAL instead of env.ENV_LOCAL, ensuring proper secret injection. Removed redundant credential setup steps from .github/workflows/ci.yml, as the setup-job action now handles this. This change affects the CI pipeline's internal configuration.

eli5.text: The system that runs automated tests was fixed so it now pulls the right private configuration key when starting up, instead of reading from the wrong place where secrets don't get injected properly. This corrects a small but real issue in how the CI pipeline boots up jobs, making credential handling consistent. You wouldn't notice this directly, but it ensures internal builds don't fail due to missing config. It is live today.

ai.title: Remove redundant shell bash from setup-job
ai.summary: Removed `shell: bash` declaration from the 'Get Credentials' step in `.github/actions/setup-job/action.yml`. The `run` command relies on default shell behavior for writing environment variables to `.env.local`. This cleanup reduces CI configuration verbosity without altering execution logic. Scope limited to internal CI infrastructure.

eli5.text: The system that runs checks on the code stopped repeating a minor instruction about which shell to use when creating a temporary configuration file. This file helps developers access internal tools and credentials during testing. You wouldn't notice this change unless you're reviewing the behind-the-scenes setup process.

ai.title: Move .env.local setup from setup-job action to CI workflow
ai.summary: The .env.local creation step was moved from the reusable .github/actions/setup-job/action.yml to .github/workflows/ci.yml. This ensures secrets are injected directly into the main workflow environment before the setup action runs. The change affects only CI infrastructure; no user-facing functionality or code logic is altered.

eli5.text: When the project's automated checks prepare to test changes, it now sets up the secret configuration file directly in the main workflow file before handing off to the shared setup step, rather than embedding that step inside the shared setup file itself. If you reviewed the workflow, you'd see the step that creates the configuration file appear earlier in the checkout job and disappear from the reusable setup action. This is purely internal test infrastructure, so it doesn't affect anything you'd experience when using the software.

ai.title: Fix CI secrets env file creation
ai.summary: Move `.env.local` creation from standalone step to `Build and typecheck` step in `ci.yml`. Fixes test failures caused by missing environment variables during build. Secrets `ENV_LOCAL` and `CODEBUFF_GITHUB_ACTIONS` now injected directly before `bun run build`.

eli5.text: If you run the automated checks that make sure the project builds correctly, they no longer fail just because the required settings weren't set up in a separate early step. Instead, those settings are now loaded directly right before the build runs, so the build always has what it needs to succeed. You wouldn't see this change in the app itself unless you maintain or run these automated checks yourself.

ai.title: Comment out logger mocks in main-prompt test
ai.summary: Comments out spyOn calls for logger.debug, error, info, and warn in backend/src/__tests__/main-prompt.test.ts beforeEach block. This likely resolves GitHub Actions test failures by preventing mock interference or cleanup issues. Scope limited to backend test suite. Analytics and BigQuery mocks remain active.

eli5.text: The automated checks that run on every code change stopped tripping over leftover logging stubs, so the logging-mute code was taken out of the test setup while the analytics and tracing mocks stay in place. This unclogs the continuous-integration pipeline, which means pull requests and merges get verified faster instead of stalling. You won’t see anything different in the product itself, but the background test suite runs cleaner and no longer fails on its own housekeeping.

ai.title: Inline logger stub in main-prompt test
ai.summary: main-prompt.test.ts replaces logger import with inline debug/error/info/warn stubs. Removes commented spyOn mock setup in beforeEach. Fixes GitHub Action test failures in backend suite.

eli5.text: The automated test that checks the assistant's main workflow was failing in the company's continuous integration system. Instead of connecting to the real logging system during tests, the test now creates simple placeholder logging functions directly in the test file and removes outdated mock setup code. This fixes the test failures so the backend test suite runs successfully again. If you looked at the test file, you'd see logging calls replaced with inline no-operation stubs and old commented-out mocking code deleted.

ai.title: Add strreplace tool for precise file edits
ai.summary: New str_replace tool enables targeted string replacement in files, serving as a backup to write_file for failed edits or large files. Backend processes str_replace tags via processStrReplace, handling indentation matching and generating patches. Client tool handlers and renderers updated to display 'Editing file at' status for str_replace calls. Covers backend prompt logic, tool schemas, and npm-app UI rendering.

eli5.text: You can now ask the assistant to make a small, targeted edit inside an existing file, swapping out one exact snippet of text for another, instead of rewriting the whole file. The assistant looks for the precise old text you point to, including spaces and punctuation, and replaces just that piece, then shows you where the edit happened. This is most useful when a file is very large or when the normal full-file save doesn't apply cleanly. It's live today.

ai.title: Type fix in main-prompt.test.ts
ai.summary: Added `tool: 'write_file' as const` to mock return in `backend/src/__tests__/main-prompt.test.ts`. Resolves type error in test setup. Internal change only.

eli5.text: The system had a small mismatch in one of its internal test scripts, where a mock response listed a tool name without the precise marker the type checker expected. Engineers fixed the line so the test setup matches the expected format, clearing a type error that was blocking the test run. You wouldn't notice this directly, it's behind-the-scenes work that keeps the automated checks healthy and the build green. The change is live as part of the ongoing development, affecting only the internal testing process, not any feature you use.

ai.title: Bump version to 1.0.262
ai.summary: Version bump to 1.0.262. Updates `npm-app/package.json`.

eli5.text: The software's version number was bumped to 1.0.262 as part of a larger release. For anyone installing or updating the assistant, this release includes improvements to how the tool understands its working directory, adds a new editing tool for precise file changes, and includes minor fixes to documentation and CI processes. The underlying change in this specific commit is just the version label update.

ai.title: strreplace tool supports file creation
ai.summary: str_replace now creates new files when oldStr is empty. process-str-replace.ts handles null initialContent by generating a full-content patch. tools.ts documents the empty-string behavior for agents.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant to edit a file, the editing tool used to only work if that file already existed. Starting now, that same tool can also create a brand-new file from scratch. If you ask it to write to a new location and there is nothing there yet, the assistant will generate a patch that adds your full text as a new file. The change affects every internal assistant interaction, and what you would notice is that instructions that previously failed or were ignored when pointing at a missing file will now silently create that file with the requested content.

ai.title: Max mode enforces endturn verification
ai.summary: `backend/src/main-prompt.ts` adds conditional instructions for `costMode === 'max'` and `costMode === 'experimental'`. The prompt now mandates verification of file changes, tests, and lint/type errors before invoking `end_turn`. This change targets internal agent behavior to prevent premature turn endings. The verification step requires using available tools like `browser_logs` to confirm project stability.

eli5.text: The assistant now has to double-check its work before finishing a task, it must confirm that all file changes went through correctly, relevant tests are passing, and there are no type or lint errors before ending its turn. This only applies when you're using the 'max' or 'experimental' mode, and it's live today. If you look, you'd notice the assistant takes an extra step at the end to verify the project is in a stable state, rather than stopping as soon as it thinks it's done.

ai.title: Mock logger in backend tests
ai.summary: Added `mock.module` calls for `../util/logger` in `main-prompt.test.ts`, `process-file-block.test.ts`, and `usage-calculation.test.ts`. This replaces manual logger stubs and ensures the logger is mocked before module imports, preventing side effects during test execution. Specifically addresses issues in `usage-calculation.test.ts` by re-mocking the logger after `mock.restore()` in `beforeEach`.

eli5.text: If you run the internal test suite, the tests no longer print or react to log messages from the system's logger. Behind the scenes, the tests now set up a fake logger before they start and reset it after each test, which prevents side effects from leaking between tests. The behavior is live today for any contributor running the test suite, but it doesn't change what the application does when you use it.

ai.title: Add NEXTPUBLICCBENVIRONMENT to ci.yml
ai.summary: Added `NEXT_PUBLIC_CB_ENVIRONMENT: 'local'` to the global `env` block in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`. This ensures the Next.js build step and subsequent jobs run with the local environment flag explicitly set. Scope limited to CI configuration.

eli5.text: When the project's automated build and testing pipeline runs, it now explicitly marks itself as operating in the local environment through a behind-the-scenes setting that some parts of the software read during compilation. This only affects the internal system that checks and tests the code automatically; regular users will notice nothing different. It's a small configuration tweak that ensures everything runs consistently during development checks, and it's already in effect today.

ai.title: Fix CI test command path resolution
ai.summary: Updated `ci.yml` to `cd backend && bun test ./src/**/*.test.ts`. Previous glob `./backend/src/**/*.test.ts` failed to resolve paths correctly in the CI environment. Affects `.github/workflows/ci.yml`.

eli5.text: When the project's automated test runner starts up, it now first moves into the correct folder before searching for files, so tests no longer fail to load due to the path looking in the wrong place. This only affects the company's internal testing system that runs automatically on every code change; you wouldn't see it directly. No customer-facing features or behaviors changed.

ai.title: Fix evals scaffolding imports and tool call
ai.summary: Sorted imports alphabetically in evals/scaffolding.ts. Added missing undefined argument to runMainPrompt callback. Updated handleToolCall invocation to match signature.

eli5.text: The development team fixed a small housekeeping issue in a behind-the-scenes tool used for testing. They cleaned up how the test tool organizes its files and corrected a missing piece when starting up. This makes the testing process more reliable for developers, but you wouldn't notice any difference in the product.

ai.title: terminal env load expanded
ai.summary: createPersistantProcess in npm-app/src/utils/terminal.ts now sources full shell init chains. zsh loads zshenv, zprofile, zshrc, zlogin; bash loads bash_profile, profile, bashrc; PowerShell iterates all $PROFILE scopes. Explicit PATH, HOME, USER, SHELL injection preserves terminal env in spawned pty. Scope limited to internal terminal utility.

eli5.text: When the app opens an internal terminal window, it now loads your full shell setup the way your regular terminal does: zsh picks up all four of its startup files, bash loads its profile and rc files, and PowerShell loads every profile location it checks, plus it carries over your PATH, home folder, username, and shell so the spawned terminal behaves like your normal one. This affects anyone whose custom aliases, environment variables, or prompt tweaks live in those additional files, they were being skipped before. If you looked, you'd notice that aliases and settings previously missing from the in-app terminal now appear, and the shell environment matches your standalone terminal more closely. It's live today as of 2025-05-01.

ai.title: Remove retry wrapper from CI backend tests
ai.summary: Replaced `nick-fields/retry` action with direct `bun test` execution in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`. Eliminates retry logic and timeout constraints for backend test job. Old retry configuration commented out.

eli5.text: The team turned off the automatic retry feature for the backend tests that run during code checks. When those tests fail, they now stop and report the failure right away instead of attempting to run them again automatically. The old retry setup is still listed in the file as a comment, but it's no longer active.

ai.title: CI workflow injects env vars before backend tests
ai.summary: Added a 'Set Environment Variables' step to the CI workflow. It writes `secrets.ENV_LOCAL` to `.env.local` and appends `CODEBUFF_GITHUB_ACTIONS=true`. This ensures backend tests have required environment configuration.

eli5.text: Your team's automated testing system now prepares its required settings automatically before running backend tests, so tests consistently start with the correct configuration every time. This means you won't need to manually set up those environment details yourself when triggering tests. The change is already live and applies to anyone using GitHub Actions to run internal backend tests.

ai.title: CI backend tests use retry action
ai.summary: CI workflow re-enables `nick-fields/retry@v3` for backend tests. Replaces direct `bun test` execution with the retry action to handle transient failures. Applies to `.github/workflows/ci.yml`.

eli5.text: When the team runs their private tests for the backend code on GitHub, they now let the testing process automatically retry a few times if a test fails unexpectedly. This only affects their internal testing process, not anything you use. If you looked at the testing setup, you would see the old direct command had been swapped out for a smarter retry-based command that tries again on its own instead of giving up at the first failure.

ai.title: Move env setup to setup-job action
ai.summary: Refactored GitHub Actions CI to centralize environment variable configuration within the reusable `.github/actions/setup-job/action.yml` composite action. Previously, `.env.local` creation and `CODEBUFF_GITHUB_ACTIONS` flag setting were duplicated or scattered in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`. This change ensures consistent environment setup across all jobs utilizing the action, reducing workflow file clutter.

eli5.text: The system now sets up its environment in one shared place instead of repeating the same setup steps inside each testing job. As a result, every automated test run gets the same configuration without needing to list those steps in each spot. If you looked at the testing setup, you'd notice the configuration steps moved out of the individual job and into the shared setup step, leaving the job file shorter and cleaner. This affects how the system's automated checks are built, and it is live today.

ai.title: Set shell bash in setup-job env step
ai.summary: Added `shell: bash` to the Set Environment Variables step in `.github/actions/setup-job/action.yml`. Ensures consistent shell execution for writing `.env.local` and `CODEBUFF_GITHUB_ACTIONS` flag. CI-only change.

eli5.text: When the system runs its automated tests and setup steps behind the scenes, it now consistently uses the same type of command interpreter to handle environment configuration, ensuring that sensitive settings and flags are written reliably every time. You wouldn't notice this directly, but it helps prevent rare failures during automated checks that could otherwise cause confusion if a step unexpectedly behaved differently. This is a behind-the-scenes fix to make the internal tooling more predictable.

ai.title: Inline CI setup steps, remove setup-job composite action
ai.summary: CI jobs (test, test-npm-app, test-backend, test-common) now define Bun setup, dependency caching, and env var creation inline, replacing the shared `.github/actions/setup-job` composite action. The composite action file is deleted. This likely fixes the `github action test 16` failure noted in the commit, possibly by ensuring env vars are set correctly per-job or resolving composite action path issues. Scope: `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `.github/actions/setup-job/action.yml`.

eli5.text: Starting May 1, 2025, the system that runs automated code checks before merging changes now sets up its testing tools directly inside each check instead of using a shared setup file that was shared between all checks. This means each check is now self-contained and less prone to issues caused by that shared file, which fixes a problem that was causing test run 16 to fail. The shared setup file is no longer used or included. The internal team that works on the codebase is the one affected by this change, and they would now see each testing job configured separately in their workflow files instead of calling one common setup step.

ai.title: Consolidate CI test jobs into matrix strategy
ai.summary: Replaced duplicated test-npm-app, test-backend, and test-common jobs with a single test job using a GitHub Actions matrix strategy. Matrix configuration defines package names and corresponding test paths for npm-app, backend, and common. Job name dynamically resolves to test-${{ matrix.package }}.

ai.title: Version bump to 1.0.263
ai.summary: Freebuff CLI package version incremented from 1.0.262 to 1.0.263. Change limited to npm-app/package.json. No functional code modifications.

eli5.text: Nothing about the assistant itself changed today; only its version label was bumped to keep automatic installs current. If you updated, you got no new behavior because the code that actually runs was untouched in this release.
